CHAPTER 901
Excavations
901.01   Permit required.
901.02   Permit application.
901.03   Permit issuance.
901.04   Permit conditions.
901.05   Exceptions.
901.06   Supervision by Public Service Director.
901.07   Obstruction of public ways.
901.08   Restoration.
901.09   Noncompliance; remedy of City.
901.10   Construction and reconstruction of utility facilities.
901.99   Penalty.
CROSS REFERENCES
      Liability for damage - see Ohio R.C. 723.49 et seq.
      Changing established grade - see Ohio R.C. 727.07
      Digging, excavating and piling dirt on street - see Ohio R.C. 5589.10
      Barricades and warning lights - see GEN. OFF.
521.03
   901.01 PERMIT REQUIRED.
   (a)    No person shall make any type of excavation in or on any street,
alley, sidewalk or public ground for any purpose whatsoever, or remove the
surface of any street within its right of way without obtaining a permit as
provided in this chapter.
   (b)    For all underground utility improvements to be installed within the
public right- of-way, applicant shall deposit with the City an amount deemed
necessary by the Director of Public Service, in no case being less than one
hundred twenty-five dollars ($125.00), prior to the issuance of a permit.
      (1)    This deposit shall be determined based upon expected costs to be
incurred by the City, including, but not limited to, plan review and on-site
inspections. These costs shall be deducted from the required deposit, above the
minimum one hundred twenty-five dollars ($125.00) which is non-refundable.
      (2)    The Director of Public Service reserves the right to require
additional deposit should the initial deposit be insufficient to cover costs
incurred by the City.
      (3)    These funds are to be held in the separate construction trust fund
by Director of Finance, and the remaining deposit, if any, shall be disbursed
to the applicant upon notification of the completion of permitted work within
thirty (30) days.
      (4)    At the discretion of the City Engineer, applicants shall be
required to remove underground utilities within the public right-of-way when
abandoned or when use otherwise ceases.
         (Ord. 2025-043. Passed 2-20-25.)
   901.02 PERMIT APPLICATION.
   Application for a permit required by Section
901.01 shall be made at the office of the Director of Public Service on forms
provided by him. The application shall show:
   (a)   The name and address of the owner or agent in charge of the property
abutting the proposed work area;
   (b)   The name and address of the party doing the work;
   (c)   The location of the work area;
   (d)   The estimated cost of the alteration; and
   (e)   Such other information as the Director finds necessary.
      (1979 Code 97.02)
   901.03 PERMIT ISSUANCE.
   The Director of Public Service shall issue a permit hereunder when he finds:
   (a)   The work will be done according to the standard specifications of the
City for public work of like character;
   (b)   The operation will not unreasonably interfere with vehicular and
pedestrian traffic, the demand and necessity for parking spaces, and the means
of ingress and egress to and from the property affected and adjacent
properties; and
   (c)   The health, welfare and safety of the public will not be unreasonably
impaired.
      (1979 Code 97.03)
   901.04 PERMIT CONDITIONS.
   In addition to the contents of the application as specified in Section
901.02, the Director of Public Service, as a condition precedent to the
granting of any permit, may require the applicant:
   (a)   To submit plans or a sketch indicating the location, size type and
duration of the excavation or removal contemplated;
   (b)   To conform with the methods of excavating, refilling and resurfacing
to be followed;
   (c)   To use those warning devices as the Director deems necessary to
protect users of the street, alley, sidewalk or public ground and abutting
property;
   (d)   To make a deposit in an amount that the Director deems necessary, in
no case being less than one hundred dollars ($100.00) or post a bond, or both,
to indemnify the City against damage as a result of the excavation or to be
used to offset required inspection service costs that result from noncompliance
to City standards. In the event the conditions of the permit are not fulfilled
or the City right of way is not restored to its original condition, the
applicant shall be given notice to make the necessary corrections and if such
corrections are not made, the City shall perform the necessary work. The
applicant shall pay for all labor and material costs associated with such work,
as well as any extra inspection costs. These costs may be deducted from the
required deposit. These funds are to be held in the separate construction trust
fund by the Director of Finance.
   (e)   To pay a fee of thirty dollars ($30.00) per utility to cover the cost
of the issuance of the permit and the cost of routine on-site inspection
services.
      (1979 Code 97.04)
   901.05 EXCEPTIONS.
   The provisions of this chapter shall not apply to any federal, state, county
or municipal employee authorized to engage in that work, or in the case of any
emergency, requiring immediate action to protect the public health, safety or
welfare.
(1979 Code 97.05)
   901.06 SUPERVISION BY PUBLIC SERVICE DIRECTOR.
   All operations for which a permit is granted hereunder shall be supervised
by the Director of Public Service.
(1979 Code 97.06)
   901.07 OBSTRUCTION OF PUBLIC WAYS.
   In removing pavement or other material from any street, alley, sidewalk or
public ground, for any purpose whatsoever, the material dug up shall be
deposited in such manner as to guard against inconvenience to the public by
obstructing any street, alley, sidewalk or public ground.
(1979 Code 97.07)
   901.08 RESTORATION.
   All places where pavement or other material is removed from any street,
alley, sidewalk or public ground shall be restored to their former condition as
speedily as practicable, either by the City or by the person causing the
pavement to be removed, as may be directed, but at the cost and expense of the
person causing the pavement to be removed.
(1979 Code 97.08)
   901.09 NONCOMPLIANCE; REMEDY OF CITY.
   Should the permittee fail or refuse to restore the street, alley, sidewalk
or public ground to the specification required by the Director of Public
Service, the Street Commissioner shall attend the restoration. The Director is
authorized to deduct, upon the statement of the Street Commissioner, the
reasonable cost of restoration and the cost of on-site inspection services at
rates prescribed in the latest contract, ordinance or resolution providing for
the services of the City Inspector from the deposit provided for in Section
901.04 and return the balance, if any, to the permittee. The remedy herein
shall be in addition to the penalty provided in Section
901.99.
(1979 Code 97.09)
   901.10 CONSTRUCTION AND RECONSTRUCTION OF UTILITY FACILITIES.
   (a)   No person shall construct, reconstruct or extend along a street, alley
or any public ground within the City any utilities without obtaining a permit
from the Department of Public Service. A utility is one of the following:
sewer, water, storm sewer, electric, natural gas, telephone, television or a
facility of similar nature. Before a permit is issued, if the Director of
Public Service deems it necessary, the applicant shall file plans and
specifications which show the course and route of the proposed utility
facilities within the City, the exact nature of the utility to be constructed,
the material, appurtenances and apparatus to be used in the construction, the
location and depth thereof and the kind and amount of energy to be transmitted,
if applicable, together with detailed specifications of the method of
transmitting or conducting the utility, and require a deposit as per Section
901.04(d). The fee for the permit shall be thirty dollars ($30.00). The release
of the deposit shall be conditioned upon the proper performance of all
conditions of the permit, if granted. Noncompliance with the conditions of the
permit shall be treated as in Section
901.04(d).
   (b)   Utilities constructed or extended to serve a new subdivision shall
comply with the City Subdivision Regulations.
   (c)   In the event emergency repairs are necessary, the work shall be
undertaken immediately and the office of the Director of Public Service shall
be notified as soon as possible of such work and a permit shall be issued
subsequent to the beginning of such repair work. Public utility companies shall
not be required to obtain a permit to work in the City right of way to perform
emergency repairs, although they are required to restore the right of way to
its original condition and to notify the City safety forces of such work.
   (d)   No permit for the construction or reconstruction of utility facilities
shall be granted if Council or the Director finds that the construction or
reconstruction would:
      (1)   Unreasonably impair the safety of the inhabitants of the City, the
general motoring public or the owners of property abutting on the streets and
ways on which the facilities are to be installed;
      (2)   Violate generally accepted standards of safe construction; or
      (3)   Otherwise adversely affect the public health, safety or welfare.
   (e)   Should Council or the Director fail to act upon an application for a
permit within thirty days after its filing, the application shall be deemed
granted and the permit deemed issued.
(1979 Code 97.10)
   901.99 PENALTY.
   Whoever violates any provision of this chapter is guilty of a misdemeanor of
the third degree.
CHAPTER 903
Annual Road Plan
903.01   Comprehensive road plan.
903.02      Annual Pavement Crack Seal Program.
   903.01 COMPREHENSIVE ROAD PLAN.
   (a)    The comprehensive road plan shall be comprised of two (2) separate
plans: a Road Maintenance Plan and a Road Improvement Plan. Each plan has a
separate purpose and different components, but collectively, both will
represent a single management plan that will ensure the City’s transportation
system is properly and well maintained.
   (b)    The comprehensive road plan will serve as a tool that allows the City
to look forward to the future to continually evaluate and improve our
transportation system.
   (c)    To facilitate the preparation of a Comprehensive Road Plan, the City
may retain the services of such professionals and/or expert consultants from
time-to-time to formulate/update a reliable Comprehensive Road Plan.
   (d)    The Mayor shall annually furnish and present to the City Council, a
Comprehensive Road Plan to be included with the submission of the annual budget
referred to in
Article III § 4 of the Stow City Charter.
   (e)    The Comprehensive Road Plan at the minimum shall contain the
following:
      (1)    A Pavement Condition Rating (PCR) Report performed in accordance
with the Ohio Department of Transportation’s Pavement Condition Rating Manual.
         A.   That a Pavement Condition Rating (PCR) be performed beginning
every three (3) years from the most current year rating performed.
         B.   The PCR shall be performed by professionals and/or expert
consultants and shall be selected using Ohio’s Qualification-Based Selection
(QBS) pursuant to Ohio Revised Code §153.65-.73.
      (2)    A street inventory containing at a minimum, the following
information:
         A.   Street names.
         B.   Approximate pavement length.
         C.   Pavement width and area.
         D.   Pavement limits.
         E.   Right-of-way width.
F.   Recent year repaved, reconstructed, maintained, etc.
         G.   Road type (local, collector, arterial, etc.).
         H.   Type of existing pavement structure (concrete, asphalt, chip
seal, gravel, etc.).
         I.   Drive apron dimensions and area.
         J.   Sidewalk, curb, curb and gutter, curb ramps and castings.
         K.   Guardrail.
         L.   Striping.
      (3)    A listing of roads expected to be reconstructed, repaired, and
maintained for each construction and repair season.
      (4)    The anticipated available funding for the upcoming paving and road
maintenance season.
      (5)    The funding mechanisms and/or means by which the anticipated and
upcoming road repairs will be funded.
      (6)    A five (5)-year Road Project Plan that prioritizes all roads and
estimated costs and funding mechanisms by year.
      
   (f)    Annually, the Administration and City Council shall determine the
method and funding to accomplish the work set forth in the Annual Road Plan for
the ensuing year.
   
   (g)    While the Comprehensive Road Plan is updated annually and subject to
change as emergencies arise or projects are delayed by circumstances beyond our
control, the annual focus primarily will be on the fifth (5th) year of the plan
as new projects are added. The first year of the plan is the basis for actual
appropriations authorized by the City Council for road projects when adopting
the Annual Budget. The remaining four (4) years establish priorities for future
road improvement projects.
(Ord. 2022-200. Passed 1-26-23.)
   903.02 ANNUAL PAVEMENT CRACK SEAL PROGRAM. 
   (a)    This Annual Pavement Crack Seal Program (Program) consists of crack
sealing city streets pursuant to the most current version of the State of Ohio,
Department of Transportation’s Construction and Material Specifications, Item
423 Crack Sealing, Hot Applied, Type IV.
   (b)    This Program will be located at various locations throughout the
municipality. The duration of crack sealing under this Program will be
determined by the Director of Public Service but shall take place sometime
between early June and mid-September and will take several weeks to complete.
   (c)    That each road and section be its own separate line item in the
bidding process paid on a ‘Lump Sum’ basis and shall follow the following
example or similar format as shown below:

      (2)    Project coordination and scheduling.
      (3)    All provisions to protect workers, the general public, and

      (4)    Reimbursement to City for costs of re-inspection or re-testing of

   (e)    That beginning January 1, 2023, and continuing thereafter, the

      (1)    Each year of this Programs existence, City streets shall be crack

      (2)    That this program be presented as part of the annual budget
process.
      (3)   Should the revenue fail to reach the amount allocated for the
Program in any given year, City Council shall conduct a review of the Program
funding to determine the funding source(s) for that year.
   (f)   The award of this program will be determined through an evaluation of
bids submitted through the City’s competitive bidding process.
(Ord. 2022-200. Passed 1-26-23.)
CHAPTER 905
Culverts, Curb Cuts and Driveways
905.01   Responsibility of owners and developers of land    fronting public
ways
905.02   Permit required.
905 03   Approach installation.
905.04   Culvert pipes required.
905.05   Historically existing obstructing culverts.
905.06   Appropriation of funds.
905.99   Penalty.
   905.01 RESPONSIBILITY OF OWNERS AND DEVELOPERS OF LAND FRONTING PUBLIC WAYS.
   The owner or developer of any newly constructed lots and lands having
frontage upon land to be used as a public right of way shall install culvert
drain pipe of a standard size and type to conform to the established street
grade over which ingress and egress may be made, after securing a permit from
the Director of Public Service for such a culvert installation. Upon failure of
the owner or developer to install the pipe, the Director or the City Engineer
shall have necessary culvert pipe installed within the right of way and in such
event the owner or developer shall pay for the installation. In the event the
costs are not paid within thirty days after billing, the same shall be
certified to the County Auditor by the Clerk of Council and assessed by the
Auditor accordingly.
(Ord. 1998-66. Passed 4-9-98.)
   905.02 PERMIT REQUIRED.
   On any street or highway wherein stone or concrete curbs are in place, no
person, other than an authorized state, county or municipal employee, shall cut
a curb for any purpose whatsoever, nor install a driveway approach or a culvert
within a public right of way, without obtaining a permit to do so as provided
in this chapter. The number of curb cuts, drive approaches and culverts shall
be limited by the Service Department to the minimum number that will provide
proper ingress and egress to the property served and to provide for needed
services.
(Ord. 1998-66. Passed 4-9-98.)
   905.03 APPROACH INSTALLATION.
   All driveway approaches shall be installed in accordance with materials and
methods standards established by the City Engineer. No work shall be undertaken
without the applicant having a working knowledge of these standards. Approaches
shall be installed so that there is a minimum of forty-eight inches from the
closest projection of a fire hydrant to the nearest edge of the approach. The
applicant shall notify the Department of Public Service, twenty-four hours in
advance of the installation for inspection.
(Ord. 1998-66. Passed 4-9-98.)
   905.04 CULVERT PIPES REQUIRED.
   The Director of Public Service and the City Engineer shall establish
standards for the construction of culvert drainage pipes in appropriate
unsewered areas throughout the City. Each owner and developer of lands
adjoining a public thoroughfare shall be responsible to contract and maintain a
drainage culvert of the size and length determined by the City Engineer to
accommodate surface water run-off adjoining the premises. The culvert shall
remain unobstructed and in good condition and shall be installed at grades
determined by the City Engineer and backfilled according to the City's design
manual. The Director shall be responsible for the installation, maintenance,
repair and replacement of culvert pipe in the event an owner or developer shall
fail to make the culvert construction herein required.
(Ord. 1998-66. Passed 4-9-98.)
   905.05 HISTORICALLY EXISTING OBSTRUCTING CULVERTS.
   Whenever the Director of Public Service or the City Engineer, upon the
exercise of his discretion, finds that a public right of way in the City
contains a historically existing culvert pipe which does not accommodate the
flow of water or which is in such a state of disrepair as to obstruct the flow
of water, the same shall be reported to Council, which may adopt a resolution
under Ohio R.C. 715.47. The resolution shall notify the owner to replace the
improper or obstructed culvert pipe with the City supplying labor to install
the same. Failing, that the City shall, two weeks after the receipt of the
notice by the owner, cause the culvert pipe to be installed assessing to the
owner of the adjoining benefited premises only the cost of the culvert pipe, at
the cost of the appropriate replacement size and length required, with labor
therefor assumed by the City. Any benefited property owner may execute a waiver
of the procedure and authorize immediate installation by the City at the
owner's cost. The amount of culvert assessment herein shall be at competitive
bid prices quoted to the City from time to time. This section shall not be
applicable to newly or recently developed lots and lands or to new subdivisions
or developments adjoining public thoroughfares. Council's determination thereof
shall be conclusive.
(Ord. 1998-66. Passed 4-9-98.)
   905.06 APPROPRIATION OF FUNDS.
   Any cost assumed by the City in connection with the authority provided for
in Sections
905.05 and
905.06 shall be consonant with the funds available and properly appropriated by
Council for that purpose.
(Ord. 1998-66. Passed 4-9-98.)
   905.99 PENALTY.
   Whoever violates any provision of this chapter is guilty of a misdemeanor of
the third degree.
(Ord. 1998-66. Passed 4-9-98.)
CHAPTER 909
Sidewalk and Curb Construction
909.01   Permit required.
909.02   Plans and specifications.
909.03   Cement required.
909.04   Inner edge to coincide with    street line.
909.05   Grade.
909.06   Width and depth.
909.07   Curb construction.
909.08   Permit fees; new construction.
909.09   Municipal Sidewalk Repair Program.
909.99   Penalty.
CROSS REFERENCES
      Construction or repair at owner's expense - see Ohio R.C. 729.01 et seq.
      Notice to construct or repair - see Ohio R.C. 729.03 et seq.
   909.01 PERMIT REQUIRED.
   No person shall construct a sidewalk within the corporate limits of the City
without obtaining a permit to do so from the Director of Public Service.
(1979 Code 97.35)
   909.02 PLANS AND SPECIFICATIONS.
   All sidewalks shall be constructed or repaired in accordance with the plans
and specifications prepared or approved by the City Engineer.
(1979 Code 97.36)
   909.03 CEMENT REQUIRED.
   All sidewalks constructed or repaired shall be of Portland Cement concrete
using limestone or slag only as aggregate material.
(1979 Code 97.37)
   909.04 INNER EDGE TO COINCIDE WITH STREET LINE.
   The inner edge of all sidewalks constructed or repaired shall coincide with
the street line unless otherwise authorized by the City Engineer.
(1979 Code 97.38)
   909.05 GRADE.
   All sidewalks shall be laid on a grade of one-half inch to the foot from the
curbline to the street line unless otherwise authorized by the City Engineer or
provided in the legislation ordering construction or repair of any specified
sidewalk.
(1979 Code 97.39)
   909.06 WIDTH AND DEPTH.
   All sidewalks shall have a minimum width of four feet and a minimum depth of
four inches. At driveway entrances, sidewalks shall have a minimum depth of six
(6) inches.
(1979 Code 97.40)
   909.07 CURB CONSTRUCTION.
   All new curbing installed within the City right of way shall be installed as
follows:
   (a)   For concrete streets, integral concrete curbs and gutters shall be
provided.
   (b)   For asphalt streets, thirty-inch concrete curbs and gutters with six-
inch vertical curb in accordance with ODOT BP.-7 type 2, shall be provided,
unless otherwise authorized by the City Engineer in writing.
      (1979 Code 97.41)
   909.08 PERMIT FEES; NEW CONSTRUCTION.
   Fees for the construction of new sidewalks and permits required therefor in
Section
909.01 are as follows:
   (a)   Where, at the discretion of the City Engineer and the Director of
Public Service, no new engineering service is required for grade or alignment
stakes, the fee shall be ten dollars ($10.00) per owner per lot.
   (b)   Where additional professional City engineering services are necessary
for setting grade stakes or alignment stakes or where other professional
engineering work or services are necessary to insure the proper construction of
sidewalks or curbs on public rights of way, whether the same is undertaken by
the City contractors or by an owner or private contractor who must avail
himself of the City Engineer's work and services, a permit fee of thirty
dollars ($30.00) shall be collected to cover the cost of the engineering
services, except when the work is to be done in a subdivision which remains
under a performance bond posted by the developer.
   (c)   If the City Engineer estimates that the necessary engineering services
will exceed the dollar amount collected in subsection (b) hereof, then the
actual expense incurred not to exceed one dollar ($1.00) per linear foot of
sidewalk or curb, shall be deposited, subject, however, to a refund of the
difference between the deposit and the actual engineering services and costs
incurred by the City Engineer, which lesser amount shall be included as an
assessable cost under a City improvement project.
   (d)   Subsections (a), (b) and (c) hereof shall have no application to, nor
shall any permit fee be charged, for sidewalk repairs.
      (Ord. 1985-141. Passed 4-11-85.)
   909.09  MUNICIPAL SIDEWALK REPAIR PROGRAM.
   The City hereby implements a Municipal Sidewalk Repair Program (“Program”)
to repair deteriorated sidewalks throughout the City. The Program shall be
divided into four (4) geographical areas per City ward, totaling sixteen (16)
areas, kept on file in the City Engineering Department and available for public
view on the City’s website.
   (a)   Inspection Frequency. Each year, the sidewalks in one geographical
area per ward will be inspected in accordance with the criteria established in
subsection (b) to determine what sidewalk repairs are necessary for the ensuing
year.
   (b)   Inspection Criteria. A City inspector will identify panels for repair
or replacement that meet one or more of the following criteria:
      (1)   The sidewalk is displaced with a vertical edge of one-half inch
(½") or more.
      (2)   The sidewalk is depressed or raised more than three (3) inches from
the normal line of grade at any place.
      (3)   The sidewalk has cracked into three (3) or more pieces, has cracks
that are between one-fourth inch (1/4") to three-fourths inch (3/4") wide or
greater or is missing a full depth piece of concrete.
      (4)   The sidewalk has spilled over seventy-five percent (75%) of the
surface.
      (5)   The sidewalk has horizontal separations equal to or greater than
three-fourths inch (3/4") within the square, or greater than one inch (1") at
the sidewalk joints.
      (6)   The sidewalk was damaged by a street tree.
      (7)   The cross slope of the sidewalk exceeds the grade established in
Section
909.05.
      (8)   Missing slabs of sidewalk.
      Sidewalks will be marked using the following symbols, denoting the
criteria for repair, and reported on a Sidewalk Inspection Report:
         C = Cracked Slab
         D = Dip or Drop in Slab
         M = Missing slabs that are required to be installed
         S = Slope of slab toward street
         T = Tree damaged slab(s)
         V = Vertical misalignment of the slab.
   (c)   Sidewalk Damaged by a Street Tree. Prior to any repairs made to slabs
damaged by a City-installed tree which is located in a treelawn, between a curb
and sidewalk, also known as “street trees”, an evaluation of the street tree
shall be performed by the City Landscape Arborist to determine any blight or
disease to the street tree.
   (d)   Curb Ramps. The Program shall have no less than eight percent (8%) of
its annual funding dedicated to bringing curb ramps into current compliance
with the Americans With Disabilities Act (ADA). All curb ramps shall be
installed in accordance with the most current Ohio Department of Transportation
(ODOT) Standard Construction Drawing BP-7.1, unless otherwise authorized by the
City Engineer, in writing.
   (e)   Program Funding. Beginning April 1, 2021, and continuing thereafter,
the Program shall be funded using revenue generated by the City’s Transient
Accommodations Tax (“Tax”). For the first year of the Program’s existence, the
calendar year 2021, the Program shall be funded in the amount of two hundred
thousand dollars ($200,000.00). Thereafter, the Program shall be funded
annually, as follows:
      (1)   To account for inflation and rising construction costs, the
Program’s funding shall be increased by two percent (2%) starting January 1,
2022, and shall be increased, annually, by said amount each calendar year
thereafter, subject to revision by the City Council in accordance with this
section.
      (2)   Each year of the Program’s existence, the sidewalks in at least one
geographical area per City ward shall be repaired as determined from the
results of previous inspections, as set forth in subsections (a) to (d).
      (3)   The Program funding set forth in subsection (e) shall be
distributed across all of the City’s geographical ward areas as equally as
possible.
      (4)   Should the tax revenue fail to reach the amount allocated for the
Program in any given year, City Council shall conduct a review of the Program
funding to determine the Program’s funding source(s) for that year.
         (Ord. 2021-58. Passed 3-31-21.)
   909.99 PENALTY.
   Whoever violates any provision of this chapter is guilty of a misdemeanor of
the third degree.
CHAPTER 913
Trees and Shrubbery
913.01   Establishment of Stow Tree    Maintenance District.
913.02   Planting prohibited without Board approval; equitable remedy.
913.03   Removal of trees on public and private property.
913.99   Penalty.
CROSS REFERENCES
      Power to regulate shade trees and shrubbery - see Ohio R.C. 715.20
      Assessments for tree planting or maintenance - see Ohio R.C. 727.011
      Injury or destruction - see GEN. OFF.
541.06
   913.01 ESTABLISHMENT OF STOW TREE MAINTENANCE DISTRICT.
   Pursuant to Ohio R.C. 715.20 and 727.011, there is established, for the
purpose of regulating the planting, trimming, maintaining and removing of trees
and other plant material in and along the public rights of way of the City,
City-owned property and open spaces and controlling blight (disease and/or
insect infestation) thereof, the Stow Tree District, also known as the City's
Urban Forest, which shall be comprised of and include all public streets within
the City, City-owned property and open spaces, and in which the planting,
trimming, caring, controlling and maintaining shall be effected. (Ord. 2010-3.
Passed 1-14-10.)
   913.02 PLANTING PROHIBITED WITHOUT BOARD APPROVAL; EQUITABLE REMEDY.
   (a)   No person shall plant any shade tree or ornamental shrubbery in or
along any public right of way unless the type or species thereof and the place
where the same is to be planted have been approved and designated by the Urban
Forestry Commission. Any shade tree or ornamental shrubbery planted without
this approval or designation may be forthwith removed by the City by written
directive of the Commission.
   (b)   The removal provided for in subsection (a) hereof shall be
accomplished at the expense of the owner of the property abutting the public
right of way wherein the unlawful planting was made, provided the planting was
made by the owner or with his consent, express or implied. Upon failure of the
owner to pay the costs, after due demand and billing the same shall be
certified to the County Auditor for placement on the owner's tax duplicate, to
be collected as other taxes are collected. The remedy provided for herein shall
be in addition to the penalty provided in Section
913.99.
   (c)   If the unlawful planting was made by someone other than the abutting
property owner and without the owner's express or implied consent, then the
removal provided for in subsection (a) hereof shall be accomplished at the
expense of the other person, the same to be collected in a civil action if the
person refuses or otherwise fails to pay the costs to the City. The remedy
shall be in addition to the penalty provided in Section
913.99.
(1979 Code 97.26)
   913.03 REMOVAL OF TREES ON PUBLIC AND PRIVATE PROPERTY.
   (a)   The Service Director or his duly authorized agent may trim any tree
existing on any public place so as to insure the safety or to preserve the
semetry or the beauty of such public place and may remove any tree or any part
thereof which is in an unsafe condition or which by reason of its location and
nature is injurious to other public improvements or is infected with any
injurious fungus, insect or other pest, which cannot otherwise be controlled.
   (b)   The Service Director or his duly authorized agent will make the final
determination on the condition of any tree or plant material.
   (c)   Whenever the Service Director or his duly authorized agent determines
that any tree located on private property has become infected with any
parasite, insect, pest or fungus so as to threaten spreading to trees standing
in any public place, or whenever the Service Director or his duly authorized
agent determines that any tree on private property in the City because of decay
or other conditions is apt to fall in whole or in part across any public
property, he shall declare the same to be a public nuisance and cause written
notice to be served upon the owner or occupant of such private property. The
notice shall order the owner or occupant to spray or otherwise treat the tree
or remove it in the manner and within the time provided in the written notice.
If the order is not complied with, the Service Director or his duly authorized
agent is authorized to enter upon such private property and to spray or
otherwise treat or remove such tree or infected or dangerous parts thereof at
the expense of the owner. The entire cost and expense of the work involved
shall be a lien on the premises and billed and collected in the manner provided
for in this chapter.
   (d)   When the Service Director or his duly authorized agent is required to
give notice to the owner or occupant of any private property to perform any
work as required by this chapter, the notice shall be in writing, shall state
the particular the nuisance, the time in which the work shall be performed and
shall contain a statement notifying the owner that if the work ordered by such
notice is not done within the time specified in the notice, then the work will
be done by the City at the expense of the owner, and that the entire cost
thereof shall be a lien upon the private property whereon such tree stands. The
notice shall also contain a statement that when the cost has been ascertained,
the owner shall be billed therefore by the City and the amount of the bill
shall be payable in cash to the Director of Finance within thirty days from
presentation to such owner. Upon failure to pay the bill, the amount thereof
together with a penalty of five percent (5%) shall be certified by the Director
of Finance to the County Auditor to be collected with other taxes for the
ensuing tax year.
    (e)   Notice shall be served personally or by certified mail to the last
known address of the owner, occupant or other person having charge of such
property. If the addresses are unknown, it shall be sufficient to publish such
notice once in a newspaper of general circulation in the City. (Ord. 2010-3.
Passed 1-14-10.)
   913.99 PENALTY.
   Whoever violates any provision of this chapter is guilty of a misdemeanor of
the third degree.
CHAPTER 917
Mailboxes
917.01   Definitions.
917.02   Visibility; obstruction.
917.03   Curbside mailbox requirements.
917.04   Cluster-style mailbox requirements.
917.05   Responsibilities of the property owner.
917.06   Responsibilities of the City and/or utility.
917.07   Protection against weather and road damage.
917.99   Penalty.
   917.01 DEFINITIONS.
   The following definitions shall apply to this chapter:
   (a)   "Breakaway support" means a supporting post which shall be no larger
than a 4" x 4" wood post or a metal post with a strength no greater than a 2"
diameter schedule 40 steel pipe and which is buried no more than 24" deep. Such
support post shall not be set in concrete unless specifically designed as a
breakaway support system as defined in "A Guide for Erecting Mailboxes on
Highways" published by the American Association of State Highway and
Transportation Officials, May 24, 1994 (AASHTO).
   (b)   "Cluster-style mailbox" means a style whereby mailboxes are assembled
together in a manufactured unit by an approved United States Postal Service
(USPS) manufacturer.
   (c)   "Curbside mailbox" means a mailbox consisting of a lightweight sheet
metal or plastic box meeting the specifications of the USPS which is erected at
the edge of a roadway or curbside of a street, is mounted on a breakaway
support post, is intended to be used for the collection of mail, and is to be
served by a carrier from a vehicle.
   (d)   "Custom-built mailbox" means a mailbox erected at the edge of a
roadway or curbside of a street constructed using materials that do not meet
the definition of a "curbside mailbox" and "breakaway support."
   (e)    "Mailbox Protection Device" means any physical guard, shield, or
deflector erected at the edge of a roadway or curbside of a street to protect a
mailbox from snow, ice, debris, or roadway maintenance impacts.
      (Ord. 2025-246. Passed 12-4-25.)
   917.02  VISIBILITY; OBSTRUCTION.
   All mailboxes must be erected:
   (a)   Away from the intersection of any street, and in no case closer than
100' measured from the centerline of the intersection, in order to prevent
obstruction of free and clear vision; and
   (b)   Away from any location where, by reason of the position, shape, or
color, it may interfere with, obstruct the view or, or be confused with any
authorized traffic control device.
      (Ord. 2009-145. Passed 7-9-09.)
   917.03  CURBSIDE MAILBOX REQUIREMENTS.
   All newly constructed or replaced curbside mailboxes shall comply with the
following installation requirements:
   (a)   The bottom of the mailbox shall be 42" from the top of the curb; on
streets without curbs, the bottom of the mailbox shall be 48" from the street
surface, as defined by USPS installation requirements.
   (b)   Lateral placement of the mailbox shall be 6" to 8" from the back of
the curb or edge of the street surface on streets without curbs, as defined by
USPS installation requirements.
   (c)   The mailbox support post shall be of a breakaway support design.
   (d)   The post-to-box attachment shall be of sufficient strength to prevent
the box from separating from the post if a vehicle strikes the post.
   (e)   The property owner shall be responsible for the maintenance of the
curbside mailbox. (Ord. 2009-145. Passed 7-9-09.)
   917.04 CLUSTER-STYLE MAILBOX REQUIREMENTS.
   All newly constructed or replaced cluster-style mailboxes shall comply with
the following installation requirements:
   (a)   The cluster-style mailbox shall be located on a concrete pad located
between the sidewalk and the curb that is at least 3' from the curb.
   (b)   The location of any cluster-style mailbox shall be approved by the
City and the USPS. For cluster-style mailboxes in new subdivisions, the
location of the mailbox shall be shown on the preliminary plat.
   (c)   The cluster-style mailbox shall have a 4' concrete access from the
public street and the public sidewalk.
   (d)   The cluster-style mailbox shall be located at the property lines on
the same side of the street that will be designated as a no parking zone.
   (e)   The cluster-style mailbox shall not be installed anywhere within a
cul-de-sac or a circular offset cul-de-sac bulb.
   (f)   The cluster-style mailbox shall not be located to conflict with any
public utilities, including, but not limited to, manholes, fire hydrants, and
intakes.
   (g)   The cost of installation of the cluster-style mailbox, including, but
not limited to, box units, the concrete pad, and the connecting sidewalk, shall
be borne by the property owner, developer, or USPS. Subsequent maintenance of
the box units and concrete pad shall be the responsibility of the USPS.
Subsequent maintenance of the connecting sidewalk shall be the responsibility
of the property owner adjacent to the sidewalk.
   (h)   No driveway or street access shall be constructed within 5' of the
cluster-style mailbox. (Ord. 2009-145. Passed 7-9-09.)
   917.05 RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE PROPERTY OWNER.
   The owner of any mailbox located in the public right-of-way after the
adoption of the ordinance codified in this chapter shall be deemed to have
agreed to the terms of this section as a condition of the owner's continued use
of the right-of-way. If a custom-built mailbox in place at the time of adoption
of the ordinance codified in this chapter is damaged beyond repair or to the
point of requiring replacement or reinstallation, the replacement mailbox must
be in compliance with this chapter. Any property owner who places any structure
or item of any kind in the right-of-way, including a mailbox, shall hold the
City harmless from any liability relating to the construction and maintenance
of the structure in the right-of-way or because of any defect therein of said
structure or noncompliance with this section. All persons, prior to installing
any mailbox in the right-of-way shall contact the Ohio Utility Protection
Service prior to beginning any work.
(Ord. 2009-145. Passed 7-9-09.)
   917.06 RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE CITY AND/OR UTILITY.
   Any type of mailbox located in the City right-of-way is subject to damage or
destruction at any time as the result of the City or a person with a utility
easement entering upon the City right-of-way to construct, repair, or maintain
facilities located in the City right-of-way, such as snow removal, pavement
repair, or street cleaning. If a curbside, cluster-style, or custom-built
mailbox located in the City right-of-way is damaged during such activities, the
City or the utility that damaged the mailbox may replace such mailbox with a
standard curbside mailbox, cluster style mailbox, or mailbox protection device
that complies with Section
 917.03,
917.04, or
917.07 of this chapter or, in the discretion of the City or utility, pay a fee
to the property owner for the repair of the mailbox or mailbox protection
device in an amount not to exceed the amount to purchase a curbside mailbox
with a breakaway support or to erect a mailbox protection device as defined in
this chapter. The Board of Control of the City of Stow shall set reimbursement
and replacement rates for mailboxes and mailbox protection devices in
compliance with this section. No property owner shall replace any nonconforming
mailbox or mailbox protection device currently installed with another
nonconforming mailbox or mailbox protection device after the effective date of
this legislation.
(Ord. 2025-246. Passed 12-4-25.)
   917.07 PROTECTION AGAINST WEATHER AND ROAD DAMAGE.
   (a)    Purpose. The purpose of this section is to establish uniform
standards for mailbox protection devices within the City. These devices are
intended to shield mailboxes from weather and road-related damage, including
snow removal operations, while ensuring public safety, visibility, and
consistency in appearance along City streets.
   (b)    Design Standards.
      (1)    Mailbox protection devices may be constructed in one of the
following configurations:
         A.    V-shaped design, positioned next to the mailbox post, forming an
angle facing the direction of oncoming traffic.
         B.    Straight design, installed parallel to the mailbox on the side
facing the direction of oncoming traffic.
      (2)    The length of the protection device shall not exceed the length of
the mailbox on any side when measured horizontally.
      (3)    The height of the protection device shall not exceed the top of
the mailbox.
      (4)    The distance between the mailbox and protective device shall be no
less than eight (8) inches and no greater than twelve (12) inches.
      (5)    The support of the protective device shall be breakaway type as
defined in this chapter, and shall use no more than three (3) such breakaway
supports.
      (6)    Devices shall be constructed of durable, weather-resistant
materials such as treated wood, plastic, or flexible composite.
      (7)    Concrete, metal, or rigid obstructions capable of causing vehicle
damage are prohibited.
      (8)    The structure shall be designed and maintained so as not to
obstruct drainage, reduce sight distance, or extend into the traveled roadway
or sidewalk.
      (9)    The address must be visible on any such protection device.
   (c)    Location and Placement.
      (1)    Mailbox protection devices shall be installed entirely within the
approved right-of-way area designated for mailbox placement by the City or the
USPS.
      (2)    Devices shall not create a hazard to pedestrians, bicyclists, or
vehicular traffic.
      (3)    The City Engineer or designee may require adjustment or removal of
any device determined to interfere with maintenance, drainage, or public
safety.
   (d)    Maintenance.
      (1)    Property owners shall be responsible for maintaining mailbox
protection devices in good repair and removing any structure that becomes
damaged, deteriorated, or noncompliant with this section.
      (2)    Any mailbox protection device installed in violation of this
section may be subject to removal by the City after written notice to the
property owner.
      (3)    Failure to correct or remove a noncompliant device within thirty
(30) days of notice may result in removal by the City at the owner's expense.
         (Ord. 2025-246. Passed 12-4-25.)
   917.99  PENALTY.
   Whoever violates any provision of this chapter is guilty of a misdemeanor of
the third degree. (Ord. 2009-145. Passed 7-9-09.)

   921.01  DEFINITIONS.
   The following definitions shall apply to this chapter:
   (a)    "Act" means the Safe Drinking water Act as amended, 42 U.S.C. 300 et
seq.
   (b)   "Contaminant" means any physical, chemical, biological or radiological
substance or matter in water.
   (c)   "City" means the City of Stow, Ohio.
   (d)   "Director" means the Director of Public Service of the City of Stow.
   (e)   "Mayor" means the chief executive officer of the municipality as
provided by the Charter of the City of Stow.
   (f)   "Person" means any individual, firm, company, municipal or private
corporation, partnership, copartnership, joint stock company, trust,
association, institution, enterprise, governmental agency, the State of Ohio,
the United States of America, or other legal entity, or their representatives,
agents, or assigns. The masculine gender shall include the feminine, the
singular shall include the plural where indicated by the context.
   (g)   "Public waterline" means a waterline provided by or subject to the
jurisdiction of the City of Stow.
   (h)   "User" means a person who receives water from a City waterline.
   (i)   "User charge" means the fee structure imposed by the City upon all
persons served by the City water system.
   (j)   "Waterline" means the pipe through which water is distributed to
users.
   (k)   "Water service connection" means the line running from the City
waterline to the user's residence or business of which the portion from the
waterline to and including the curb box shall be owned and maintained by the
City and the portion from the curb box to the user's structure shall be owned
and maintained by the user.
   (l)   "Water system" means all the facilities for the treating, pumping,
storing and distribution of potable water. It shall not include plumbing inside
buildings or the line running from a building to the curb box.
      (Ord. 2001-161. Passed 10-25-01.)

by Ordinance No. 2001-109, the City has established a water system located
within the City of Stow and parts of the City of Hudson serving the City of
Stow and a portion of the Cityof Hudson.
   (b)   The administration is hereby authorized to establish rules and
regulations within the parameters of this chapter for the purpose of managing
the day-to-day operations of the City water distribution system.
(Ord. 2001-161. Passed 10-25-01.)

   921.04 FIRE PROTECTION SERVICE.
   (a)   A fire protection system shall be connected to a City water line in
order to establish fire protection service. The water service line does not
require a meter when it is dedicated exclusively to a fire protection system
and/or fire hydrant. A fire protection system within a building shall be
equipped with an automatic alarm that sounds either inside the building,
outside the building or to a central alarm station and it shall activate
whenever water is passing through the system. Installations involving detector
check valves shall be billed as unmetered service. Detector check valves are to
be provided by the owner and shall be a brand and model approved by the City of
Stow.
   (b)   Where metered fire protection systems exist, in addition to the
monthly rate specified in subsection (c) hereof, the owner shall pay for water
used through such line(s) at the rates established in Section
921.03(b) less the billing charge.
   (c)   All customers with fire protection service shall be charged a monthly
fee. The Fee shall vary depending on the largest sized pipe diameter used
within the fire protection system and whether the service is metered or
unmetered as follows, effective with the billing sent to customers in the first
month after the effective date of this section. Subsequent increases will occur

   921.05 HYDRANT CHARGES.
   The City does not permit the commercial or private use of its hydrants.
   (a)   No person shall take water from any public hydrant.
   (b)   Bulk water is available to private individuals or commercial
endeavors. Application must be made with the Water Maintenance Division. Access
is restricted to a designated site and must be hauled by the purchaser.
   (c)   Bulk water rates are currently set at $10.00 per 1,000 gallons."
      (Ord. 2014-112. Passed 9-11-14.)
   921.06 BILLING.
   (a)   The charges established in this chapter shall be billed monthly and
shall be payable by the due date specified on the billing statement. Payments
shall be applied to delinquent balances first and the remainder to current
charges. Current charges not paid by the due date shall be deemed delinquent
and an additional charge of ten percent (10%) of the delinquent current charge
shall be added each month to the amount due. A charge of ten dollars ($10.00)
shall be added for all checks returned from financial institutions for
nonsufficient funds.
   (b)   Delinquent charges may be certified to the County Auditor and placed
on the real property tax list and duplicate against the property served by the
water connection. All accounts certified to the County Auditor for collection
shall be subject to a certification charge of ten percent (10%) of the
delinquent amount which shall be added to the amount certified. The total
charge shall be a lien on the property from the date it is placed on the real
property tax list and duplicate by the Auditor and shall be collected in the
same manner as other taxes.
   (c)   Refunds and Abatements. The Director of Finance shall have the
authority to authorize refunds or abatements on a bill for metered water for
one of the following reasons:
      (1)   Where an error has been made in the reading of the meter or the
preparation of the bill.
      (2)   When the meter, upon testing, shows an average over-registration
greater than two percent (2%).
      (3)   When any charge of the City water billing operation has been paid
twice or incorrectly.
   (d)   No refunds will be made based on estimated readings. In general, all
overpayments will be credited to the account and shown as a credit against the
account on the next bill rendered.
   (e)   Billing Disputes and Adjustments. The Director of Finance shall have
the authority to make final determinations regarding billing disputes and to
make legitimate billing adjustments based upon reasonable standards adopted in
accordance with Water System rules and regulations
established pursuant to Section
921.01, herein.
(Ord. 2001-161. Passed 10-25-01.)
   921.07 SERVICE DISCONTINUANCE AND RESUMPTION.
   (a)   The supply of water through any service may be discontinued by the
Stow Service Department for:
      (1)   Use of water on any premises other than that specified on the
application.
      (2)   Willful waste of water through improper, imperfect or worn out
pipes or fixtures.
      (3)   Failure to properly maintain connections, service pipes or fixtures
owned by the user.
      (4)   Cross-connection or interconnection with any other supply of water.
      (5)   Installation of pipe or fixtures which may permit back siphonage or
backflow.
      (6)   Tampering with any service line, meter, curb stop, corporation stop
or seal, or any other City water appurtenance.
      (7)    Nonpayment of water charges.
      (8)   Failure to provide reasonable access to install, read or remove a
water meter for four consecutive months.
      (9)   Making additions or alterations to service lines prior to the water
meter without written permission.
      (10)   Failure to execute a water contract.
      (11)   Any structure determined to be vacant.
   (b)   Before water service is discontinued, a diligent effort shall be made
to notify the user of the pending action. Notice may be provided to the owner
of the property or to the tenant or occupant of the premises in writing, in
person, by telephone, or by posting of a notice on the premises. In the event
of a water main break or other emergency, water service may be discontinued
without notice.
   (c)   The water service shall not be turned on until the cause of
discontinuance has been removed and all charges have been paid or otherwise
resolved.
(Ord. 2001-161. Passed 10-25-01.)
   921.08 WATER TAP-IN CAPACITY FEE.

   921.09  WATER SERVICE FEES.
   All users in the City Water System shall pay one or more of the
following water service fees prior to connection to a City water line:
   (a)   Inspection fee for water service 2” or less includes the inspection of
all work from the water tap to the meter:
ENGINEERING INSPECTION FEE*
 
Short side $225.00
Long side  $350.00
   (b)   Water meter fees:
WATER METER FEE
 
5/8" meter $260.00*
3/4" meter $310.00*
1" meter   $365.00*
1 ½" meter$600.00*
2" meter   $800.00*
      * Owner must provide backflow preventer, if required.
   Larger meters shall be provided to the owner by the City of Stow and the fee
shall be the City's invoice amount plus (20%) twenty percent.
   (c)   Pre-existing water taps: A fee of $400.00 will be charged for any
residential water service tap installed prior to 11/7/01 if the fee for that
tap was not previously paid to the Summit County Department of Environmental
Services. In the event of a dispute of payment by the property owner, the issue
shall be resolved by producing an original receipt for such payment; otherwise,
payment shall be made to the City of Stow.
   (d)   Water service disputes may exist for those applicants to whom the
Summit County Department of Environmental Service issued a sewer permit, but
would not issue a water permit. The City of Stow Board of Control is authorized
to resolve water service fee disputes that are associated with sewer permits
issued from October 1, 2001 through November 7, 2001.
(Ord. 2006-57. Passed 4-12-06.)
 
   921.10  MISCELLANEOUS WATER SERVICE FEES.
       Residences or businesses located within the geographic area served by
the City of Stow Water Department that utilize private wells as a water source
shall have the opportunity to meter their systems for the purposes of billing
for sanitary sewer charges. Potential private well customers shall pay the
current purchase price plus 10% as a one-time service charge. The City shall
retain ownership of all meters in its system and will assume responsibility for
their maintenance and repair. Any repairs or replacements caused by customer
neglect or malicious damage will be at the owner's expense. Exterior reading
equipment is required on all metered services. These devices will be installed
by the Water Division and placed in an easily accessible location. All interior
plumbing to accommodate the installation of a meter will be done at the private
owner's expense and must be in place before a meter is installed. All interior
plumbing must meet current City of Stow specifications and is subject to
inspection by the City of Stow.
(Ord. 2014-112. Passed 9-11-14.)
 
   921.11 CONSTRUCTION SERVICE FEE.
   (a)   All persons constructing privately financed water projects intended to
become part of the City Water System shall pay a construction service fee for
engineering, inspection and administrative functions performed by the City.
(Ord. 2001-161. Passed 10-25-01.)
   (b)   The following service fee shall be paid at the time of the pre-
construction conference after the City Engineer has approved the project for
construction, which approval shall be valid for a period of one (1) year.
      Water Distribution Lines - (6" diameter water line & above):
      $3.10 per lineal foot constructed.
(Ord. 2006-57. Passed 4-12-06.)
 
   (c)   Requests for overtime inspection service shall be approved by the City
Engineer and shall be billed at the rate of fifty dollars ($50.00) per hour.
Overtime shall be accrued in one- half hour increments only. Overtime is any
time worked outside of normal business hours.
(Ord. 2001-161. Passed 10-25-01.)
   921.12  AGREEMENTS FOR CONSTRUCTING PRIVATELY FINANCED WATER LINES.
   (a)   When the following procedures, as stated in this Chapter
921 have been adhered to, the Mayor may execute an agreement on behalf of the
City:
      (1)   Upon request from a private developer to extend the City water
lines, the Mayor shall have an agreement prepared for signature with the
conditions set forth.
      (2)   The Department of Engineering shall review and approve the plans
and specifications for the proposed water line extension.
      (3)   The developer shall follow the established guidelines and standards
outlined in this Chapter
921.
      (4)   The developer shall be responsible for any and all costs associated
with the construction or extension of the proposed water line.
      (5)   After construction of the proposed water lines, all applicable fees
for services offered by the City shall be followed as established in this
Chapter
921.
   (b)   In any instance where the City is participating in the cost of the
improvements through requested over-sized lines, purchases facilities, replaced
and enlarged lines, etc., the Law Director shall prepare, for Council
authorization by resolution, an agreement to be entered into between the Mayor
and the developer specifying the maximum reimbursement due the developer. (Ord.
2001-161. Passed 10-25-01.)
   921.13 CONNECTIONS TO CITY WATER MAIN THROUGH EASEMENT ON ADJOINING
PROPERTY; WHEN PERMITTED; ASSESSMENT.
   (a)   All buildings seeking connection to the City Water System shall be
served with water only through a service from the main in the street or
dedicated utility right-of-way on which the lot has frontage, except that when
there is no main in the street or dedicated utility right-of-way and a proper
connection can be made elsewhere on adjoining property, the owner of the lot
may, after obtaining a recorded easement from the owner of a lot on an
adjoining street or dedicated utility right-of-way and paying the current front
foot connection charge based on the width of his property as called for under
Chapter
921, obtain water through said easement from the adjoining street or dedicated
utility right-of-way. The owner of the lot to be benefited by such easement
shall furnish a copy of the recorded easement to the Department of Public
Service prior to installation of the line; said easement shall contain a clear
reference to this codified section so as to put future property owners on
notice and shall be required even if both lots are currently owned by the same
person or entity. Upon proper application, the Department of Public Service
shall permit the installation of a curb meter and curb box on the adjoining
street or dedicated right-of-way. The benefited property owner shall be
responsible for the design and installation of the waterline, all of which
shall be subject to inspection by the City of Stow and any fees thereof. The
benefited property owner shall be responsible for maintaining the waterline
after installation. Additionally, said property owner shall be required to
deposit a fee of five hundred dollars ($500.00) to the City of Stow at the time
of connection to the main in the adjoining street or dedicated utility right-
of-way. When a main is laid in the street or dedicated right-of-way on which
the lot has frontage, the owner shall be required to purchase a standard
service from the new main or dedicated utility right-of-way and disconnect the
service from the main in the adjoining street or dedicated utility right-of-
way. Connection to the new main shall be designed and installed by the City of
Stow at the benefited property owner's expense. The property owner shall be
responsible for the cost per linear foot for the frontage of the property as
obtained by the City of Stow, less the five hundred dollar ($500.00) previously
deposited with the City of Stow. The cost for connection to the new main may be
paid in full or assessed to property owner's taxes over a period of time not to
exceed five years.
   (b)   This section shall be supplemental to and not in derogation of
existing ordinances relative to water connections required for any building
within the City.
(Ord. 2015-71. Passed 7-9-15.)
   921.14 OPT-IN PROGRAM FOR WATERLINE INSTALLATION IN RESIDENTIAL AREAS.
   (a)    This program shall be operated by the City of Stow Department of
Public Service. Locations of newly installed waterlines shall be at the sole
discretion of the Department of Public Service, based on water quality issues,
overall cost, and potential customers; initially and in the future.
   (b)   The Department of Public Service shall hold a neighborhood meeting,
upon request from a homeowner(s) for installation, to determine interest and
viability of potential tap-ins. At such meeting, residents shall be provided a
construction estimate to assist in determining potential cost. The construction
estimate provider at such a meeting reflects the best estimate at the beginning
of the project and is non-binding.
   (c)   This program shall be opt-in only. No resident will be mandated to tap
into the City water system.
   (d)    Residents wishing to tap-in at the time of construction must notify
the City prior to the commencement of construction. Nothing in this Section
will prohibit residents to tap-in at any other time. Residents who do not
notify the City prior to the commencement of construction will not be
considered to have tapped in at the time of construction and the benefits
contained therein, as described in subsection (h) and will be considered under
subsection (i) of this Section.
   (e)   The City will mail letters to all eligible residents prior to
commencement of construction in order to inform them of the opportunity to opt-
in to the program. The City shall send these notice letters via U.S. Mail at
the earliest reasonable time period.
   (f)   Upon completion of the project, a final construction cost shall be
certified by the City’s Engineering Department. This certified cost shall be
kept in perpetuity by the City and shall be utilized to calculate all future
benefit costs for eligible residents under this Program.
   (g)   This certified construction cost will be used to calculate the total
cost of the Project. The total cost of the project shall be divided according
to each benefit or potential benefit at the time of construction completion.
These benefits and potential benefits shall also be certified by the City
Engineer and shall be kept in perpetuity by the City.
   (h)    Tap-In At the time of Construction.
      (1)   Residents choosing to tap into the main line at the time of
construction shall be responsible for seventy five percent (75%) of the cost of
their individual benefit. This individual benefit, for Residents choosing to
tap into the main line at the time of construction, cost shall not exceed five
thousand dollars ($5,000).
      (2)   Residents choosing to tap into the main line at the time of
construction shall also be required to pay for the cost of their meter at the
rate previously established by legislation of Stow City Council.
      (3)   Inspection fees shall be waived for residents choosing to tap into
the main line at the time of construction.
            
   (i)    Tap-In After the time of Construction.
      (1)   Residents that choose not to tap in at the time of construction,
but choose to do so at a later date, shall be charged seventy-five percent
(75%) of the cost of their benefit. Properties that choose not to tap in at the
time of construction, but choose to do so at a later date, shall be charged a
maximum individual benefit in an amount not to exceed five thousand dollars
($5,000), plus the cost of a meter as previously established by Stow City
Council, and all associated inspection fees.
      (2)   Residents choosing to tap into the main line after the time of
construction shall also be required to pay for the cost of a meter as
previously established by Stow City Council.
      (3)   Residents choosing to tap into the main line after the time of
construction shall also be required to pay for all associated inspection fees.
   (j)    It shall be the responsibility of each resident to install the
service line from the main line to the residence and bear one hundred percent
(100%) of the associated costs. All associated work must follow all other
requirements found under this Code. Work performed on service lines will fall
outside of the parameters of this program. The City shall not be a party to
such agreements made between the homeowner and their chosen contractor.
   (k)   Service lines for homes choosing to tap in at the time of construction
shall be subject to inspection by the City despite the waiving of inspection
fees.
   (l)   Invoicing.
      (1)   Invoicing for this program shall be performed by the City of Stow
Department of Public Service.
      (2)   Residents shall have the option to pay all fees and charges for
this program at the time the construction cost is certified by the Engineering
Department or through invoicing. Should the resident choose invoicing,
residents will be invoiced annually over a period of not more than ten (10)
years to repay the City assessment for this program, with appropriate interest
being determined at the execution of the repayment agreement (as determined by
the City) and charged for the period of the repayment. The City may determine
the appropriate method of repayment agreement. There shall be no penalty for
early payoffs.
      (3)   An administrative fee of three percent (3%), in addition to the
repayment interest amount, shall be charged by the City for residents choosing
to be assessed by the City for the project over a period of years in the
future.
      (4)   Non-payment of the charges shall be submitted to Summit County for
normal tax assessment through the property tax bills or to the Attorney
General's office for further collection efforts, as determined by the City.
         (Ord. 2023-160. Passed 10-26-23.)
CHAPTER 923
Water System Backflow/Cross Connection Control
923.01   Purpose and policy.
923.02   Definitions.
923.03   Backflow and cross connections prohibited.
923.04   Survey and inspection.
923.05   Systems requiring protection.
923.06   Type of protection required.
923.07   Backflow protection on fire suppression systems.
923.08   Backflow prevention assemblies.
923.09   Installation.
923.10   Inspection and maintenance.
923.11   Booster pumps.
923.12   Violations.
CROSS REFERENCES
Backflow - see OAC 4101:2-51-38
   923.01  PURPOSE AND POLICY.
   (a)   Purpose. The purpose of this chapter is to establish guidelines
concerning the protection of the public potable water supply from contamination
or pollution by isolating within the consumer's water system contaminants or
pollutants which could backflow through the service connection into the public
potable water system. Further, provisions are made for the maintenance of a
continuing program of cross-connection control which will systematically and
effectively prevent the contamination or pollution of the public and consumer's
potable water system.
   (b)   Policy. The Director of Public Service shall be responsible for the
protection of the public potable water system from contamination due to
backflow of contaminants through the water service connection. If, in the
judgment of the Director, an approved backflow prevention device is necessary
at the water service connection to any consumer's premises for the safety of
the water system, the Director or his authorized representative shall give
notice to the consumer to install such approved backflow prevention device at
each service connection to his premises. The consumer shall install such
approved device or devices at his own expense within thirty (30) calendar days
of written approval. Any failure, refusal or inability on the part of the
consumer to install such device or devices immediately shall constitute grounds
for discontinuing water service to the premises until such device or devices
have been installed.
(Ord. 2001-161. Passed 10-25-01.)
   923.02 DEFINITIONS.
   (a)   The following definitions shall apply to this chapter.
      (1)   "Air gap separation" means the unobstructed vertical distance
through the free atmosphere between the lowest opening from any pipe or faucet
supplying water to a tank, plumbing fixture, or other device and the flood
level rim of the receptacle.
      (2)   "Approved" means that a backflow prevention device or method has
been accepted by the supplier of water and the Director of Public Service as
suitable for the proposed use.
      (3)   "Auxiliary water system" means any water system on or available to
the premises other than the public water system and includes the water supplied
by the system. These auxiliary waters may include water from another supplier's
public water system; or water from a source such as wells, lakes, or streams;
or process fluids; or used water. They may be polluted or contaminated or
objectionable or constitute a water source or system over which the supplier of
water does not have control.
      (4)   "Backflow" means the flow of water or other liquids, mixtures, or
substances into the distributing pipes of a potable water supply from any
source other than the intended source of the potable water supply.
      (5)   "Backflow prevention device" means any device, method or type of
construction intended to prevent backflow into a potable water system.
      (6)   "Consumer" means the owner or person in control of any premises
supplied by or in any manner connected to a public water system.
      (7)    "Consumer's water system" means any water system, located on the
consumer's premises, supplied by or in any manner connected to a public water
system. A household plumbing system is considered to be a consumer's water
system.
         (Ord. 2001-161. Passed 10-25-01.)
   923.03  BACKFLOW AND CROSS CONNECTIONS PROHIBITED.
   (a)   No water service connection shall be installed or maintained to any
premises where actual or potential cross connections to the public potable or
consumer's water system may exist, unless such actual or potential cross
connections are abated or controlled to the satisfaction of the Director of
Public Service or his authorized representative.
   (b)   The Director of Public Service may order the installation of an
approved backflow prevention assembly or method at the water service connection
(s) to control backflow from the premises.
   (c)   The owner/consumer shall install the designated assembly or method at
his own expenses. Failure, refusal or inability to install said assembly or
method shall constitute a justification for discontinuing water service to the
premises until such assembly or method has been installed and approved.
   (d)   The use of the approved backflow preventer at the water service
connection does not in any way affect or eliminate the need for individual
fixture devices or air-gaps as required by the Ohio Plumbing Code. (Ord. 2001-
161. Passed 10-25-01.)
   923.04 SURVEY AND INSPECTION.
   (a)   The consumer's premises shall be open at all reasonable times to City
inspectors for the conduction of surveys and investigations of water use
practices within the consumer's premises to determine whether there are actual
or potential cross connections to the consumer's water system through which
contaminants or pollutants could backflow into the public potable water system.
Such investigations are authorized by Ohio Administrative Code 3745-95-03.
   (b)   On request by City inspectors, the consumer shall furnish information
on water use practices within the consumer's premises.
(Ord. 2001-161. Passed 10-25-01.)
   923.05 SYSTEMS REQUIRING PROTECTION.
   (a)   An approved backflow prevention assembly shall be installed on each
service line to a consumer's water system serving premises where any of the
following conditions exist or are proposed:
      (1)   An auxiliary water supply (domestic or fire);
      (2)   An actual or potential hazard to the public potable water system;
      (3)   Internal cross connections;
      (4)   Intricate plumbing arrangements, which make it impractical to
determine whether or not cross connections exist;
      (5)   Repeated history of cross connections;
      (6)    Any reason it is not possible to make a complete inspection; and
      (7)   Others specified by the Director of Public Service or the Director
of the Ohio Environmental Protection Agency.
   (b)   Any heating, ventilating and air conditioning (HVAC) equipment or
process system with chemical additives shall have an approved backflow
prevention assembly installed on the system. If said assembly is not installed,
the Director of Public Service or his authorized representative may order the
installation of an approved backflow prevention assembly on the service line to
the premises.
   (c)   No connection shall be installed or maintained whereby an auxiliary
water supply may enter the public potable or consumer's water system unless
said auxiliary water supply and the method of connection and use of said supply
shall have been approved by the Director of Public Service and by the Director
of the Ohio Environmental Protection Agency as required by Ohio R.C. 6109.13.
(Ord. 2001-161. Passed 10-25-01.)
   923.06  TYPE OF PROTECTION REQUIRED.
   (a)   The type of protection required shall depend on the degree of hazard.
The minimum requirements are as follows:
      (1)   An approved air-gap separation shall be installed in special cases
where there could be a severe health hazard. Such determination shall be made
by the Director of Public Service or his authorized representative.
      (2)   An approved reduced pressure principle backflow prevention assembly
shall be installed where a public water system may become contaminated.
      (3)   An approved double check valve assembly shall be installed where a
public water system may be polluted.
         (Ord. 2001-161. Passed 10-25-01.)
   923.07 BACKFLOW PROTECTION ON FIRE SUPPRESSION SYSTEMS.
   (a)   An approved reduced pressure principle detector assembly shall be used
on the following types of fire suppression systems:
      (1)   All foam-water fire suppression systems;
      (2)   Systems with an auxiliary water supply; and
      (3)   Systems with chemical additives.
   (b)   An approved double detector check assembly shall be used on all other
types of fire suppression systems not mentioned above.
(Ord. 2001-161. Passed 10-25-01.)
   923.08  BACKFLOW PREVENTION ASSEMBLIES.
   Any backflow prevention assembly installed shall be of an approved make and
model, as defined in Section
923.02(a)(5). Existing backflow prevention assemblies approved by the Director
of Public Service or the Ohio Environmental Protection Agency at the time of
installation and properly maintained shall be considered approved.
(Ord. 2001-161. Passed 10-25-01.)
   923.09 INSTALLATION.
   (a)   Backflow prevention assemblies shall be installed at an approved
location and in an approved manner. Where the manufacturer's specifications for
installation conflict with Ohio Environmental Protection Agency standards, Ohio
EPA standards shall prevail.
   (b)   Backflow prevention assemblies installed on the service line to a
consumer's water system shall be located on the consumer's side of the water
meter, as close to the meter as is reasonably practical and prior to any other
connection.
(Ord. 2001-161. Passed 10-25-01.)
   923.10 INSPECTION AND MAINTENANCE.
   (a)   It shall be the duty of the owner/consumer at any premises on which
backflow prevention assemblies are installed to have inspection, tests and
overhaul made in accordance with the following schedule, or more often:
      (1)   Air-gap separation shall be inspected at time of installation and
at least every twelve (12) months thereafter.
      (2)   Reduced pressure principle backflow prevention assemblies shall be
inspected and tested at the time of installation and at least every twelve (12)
months thereafter. They shall be dismantled, inspected internally, cleaned and
repaired whenever needed, and at least every five (5) years.
      (3)   Double check valve assemblies shall be inspected and tested at the
time of installation and at least every twelve (12) months thereafter. They
shall be dismantled, inspected internally, cleaned and repaired whenever
needed, but at least every two (2) years.
   (b)   Inspections, tests and overhaul of backflow prevention assemblies
shall be made at the expense of the water consumer and shall be performed by a
person approved by the Director of Public Service or his authorized
representative and certified by the Ohio Department of Health as qualified to
inspect, test and overhaul backflow prevention assemblies. Whenever an air gap
or backflow prevention assembly required by these regulations are found to be
defective, they shall be repaired or replaced at the expense of the consumer
without delay.
   (c)   The water consumer must maintain a complete record of each backflow
prevention assembly from purchase to retirement. This shall include a
comprehensive listing of al tests, inspections and repairs. Records of
inspections, tests, repairs and overhaul shall be submitted to the Service
Department at least yearly.
   (d)   Backflow prevention assemblies shall not be bypassed, made
inoperative, removed or otherwise made ineffective without specific written
authorization by the Director.
(Ord. 2001-161. Passed 10-25-01.)
   923.11 BOOSTER PUMPS.
   (a)   Where a domestic or fire booster pump has been installed on the
service line to or within any premises, said pump shall be equipped with a low
pressure cut-off device to shut off the booster pump when the pressure in the
service line on the suction side of the pump drops to ten (10) pounds per
square inch gauge or less.
   (b)   The low pressure cut-off device shall be installed, tested and
maintained in a manner acceptable to the Director of Public Service.
(Ord. 2001-161. Passed 10-25-01.)
   923.12  VIOLATIONS.
   (a)   The Director of Public Service shall deny or discontinue the water
service to any premises where there has been any violation of the backflow/
cross connection control rules outlined in this chapter. Said discontinuance of
supply is authorized by Ohio Administrative Code 3745-95-08. Such action shall
be taken after reasonable notice to the consumer except where an imminent
health risk or emergency necessitates immediate action by the Service
Department.
   (b)   Water service to said premises shall not be restored until the
consumer has complied with these regulations to the satisfaction of the
Director or his authorized representative.
(Ord. 2001-161. Passed 10-25-01.)
